findings.claim: Aborting the supplied signal during client-tool execution still permits subsequent graph writes and marks the run finished.
findings.evidence: stream() checks signal.aborted before await this.apply(event, run), but RUN_FINISHED awaits runClientTools(run), whose post-execution guard checks only run.isCurrent(). If the supplied AbortSignal is aborted while provider.executeTool() is pending, the run remains current, so its tool result is written, additional tools can execute, and RUN_FINISHED writes runStatus: "finished". The cancellation check after the stream loop cannot correct this because it only handles a record still marked "running".
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the run's AbortSignal into tool execution and check it before starting each tool and after every awaited tool execution. On cancellation, stop processing and mark the still-current run cancelled without writing late tool results.

findings.claim: Asynchronous renderer-message delivery failures escape as unhandled promise rejections.
findings.evidence: CreatePrometheusA2uiRuntimeOptions explicitly permits onRendererMessage to return Promise<void>, and sendRendererMessage awaits it. reportV1Failure calls void this.sendRendererMessage(...) inside a synchronous try/catch, which cannot catch a rejected promise; forwardSurfaceErrors also discards that promise without a rejection handler. A rejecting transport callback therefore produces an unhandled rejection while reporting a protocol or surface error.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach a rejection handler to fire-and-forget renderer-message deliveries and report delivery failures through an explicit host error channel without replacing the original protocol error or recursively sending another renderer message.
